eligibility.quote: Topic `mavros/global_position/gp_origin` has type `geographic_msgs/GeoPointStamped` and must contain coordinates in LLA. When I send a request containing LLA, I expect to receive a response containing LLA too in order to compare it and ensure that global_origin has been successfully set.
eligibility.reason: E1/E4 are supported by the concrete coordinate round trip and code. The MAVROS plugin publishes ECEF-valued fields to an external client expecting LLA: an erroneous representation crosses a topic boundary in PAIR. E2 step 2 explicitly includes wrong values crossing a boundary even if the resolving edit is internal to the provider. It is not an internal-only defect.

missed_conditions.quote: It is highly counter intuitive to send ECEF coordinates in a ROS message, that is only intended to be used with LLA coordinates:
missed_conditions.reason: Cartesian ECEF components are encoded in a geographic latitude/longitude/altitude message. The same named type remains in use; this is neither a nominal-type mismatch nor a renamed element. These elements must be added to the currently null inventory; the leading slash assumes the namespace illustrated by the report.

loudness.quote: Then FCU confirms this with GPS_GLOBAL_ORIGIN message containing the same coordinates as LLA. But plugin transforms it to ECEF and sends to topic `mavros/global_position/gp_origin`.
loudness.reason: The specification leaves this null after incorrectly excluding the case. The source reports wrong published data, without a build, connection, or activation diagnostic.

detection_stage.quote: But plugin transforms it to ECEF and sends to topic `mavros/global_position/gp_origin`.

resolution.quote:
However the messages are published in ECEF coordinates.
This PR removes such conversion matching message requirements and message contents.
resolution.reason: The merged fix removes the LLA-to-ECEF conversion. No successful rerun with the reporter's revision-identified external client is shown.

notes: The external client is described by its requests and expected responses, not a public repository. Its existence and expectation are explicit in the report. A reference-frame label of earth does not distinguish Cartesian ECEF from geographic LLA; the representation convention is the best-supported classification.
